newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures up as rate rumours discounted.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures up as rate rumours discounted.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Friday as recent fears of a rise in Japanese interest rates faded from the market, dealers said.
"I think the market has discounted the whole thing," said a Singapore-based futures dealer. "The stock market, at least, believes Japanese government policy is for no rate change."
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract closed 370 points higher at 21,210. It earlier rose to a high of 21,250.

The contract fell on Thursday after an official at Japan's Ministry of Finance, Eisuke Sakakibara, said the Japanese economy was stronger than the market thought and that the dollar's correction was about to finish.
The remarks sparked a sharp fall in the dollar and a slide in Euroyen and Japanese government bond futures.
"I think today's rise was just short-covering," said a Japanese dealer.
A chartist with a U.S. trading house said the December Nikkei appeared to be range-trading between a low of 20,750 and a high of 21,300.
"Today's close at 21,210 may be a good sign," he said. "It may try to take out the 21,300 level next week."
